display: I'm a board-certified music therapist (MT-BC) with a new private practice in Leslieville, Toronto, specializing in autistic children aged 4-12.

signals.text: I just opened a private practice in Leslieville and I'm looking for more families who could use music therapy.
I'd like to run a monthly Saturday-morning singing-and-talking group for parents of newly diagnosed children, and I need to know whether my room can handle a group.
I'm still looking for a decent acoustic piano, ideally an upright, because it matters for how I work and a keyboard isn't the same.
My whole setup budget was about $3,800, and used uprights run $3,000-4,500 plus moving, so I'm watching for free or cheap pianos.
I still need a few things for the room: curtains, a rug and a small cabinet, all cheap or secondhand.
I'm building up from a handful of clients a week and aiming for about ten to be comfortable.
I miss having colleagues and a team around, such as an OT room to share ideas with.
I'm anxious about money and sometimes wonder whether leaving a steady job was reckless, though I feel most certain when I'm in the work.
I'm tentatively and happily starting something new in my personal life after a long relationship ended.
I'm saving seeds and tending a balcony garden, and I find it hopeful.

offers.text: Music therapy sessions for autistic children aged 4-12, delivered by an MT-BC with a Master's in Music Therapy from Wilfrid Laurier.
Nine years of clinical experience in a children's hospital developmental unit.
Guitar, keyboard, hand drums and voice, with a small Orff instrument set and a gathering drum.
Singing and talking facilitation for parent groups.
A sound-sealed 14 x 11 ft room with natural light above a bookshop in Leslieville, suitable for small-group work.
Can explain what music therapy is in plain language to parents, teachers and clinicians, including at info nights.
I speak English and some French, with a little Igbo.

catchers.hypo: Hi, we're clearing out an old upright piano and want it to go to someone who will use it, not a dump. Could you use it?
catchers.can: I'd gladly take it and use it in sessions where children can feel the vibration through the soundboard, and I can arrange the moving.
catchers.confirm: Is the piano an acoustic upright, or a grand or digital instrument, that is free or low-cost and can be moved within Toronto?

catchers.hypo: My child was just diagnosed with autism and I don't know where to start. Do you know of a group or a person to talk to?
catchers.can: I can invite them to the planned parent group, or point them to the right kind of session.
catchers.confirm: Is the child aged 4-12 and are you in or near Toronto?

catchers.hypo: I'm an OT, SLP or school professional looking for a music therapist to refer children to, or to co-run a session.
catchers.can: I can take referrals or co-plan sessions, and I'd welcome the colleagueship.
catchers.confirm: Are you a licensed clinician or school professional in the Toronto area who needs a music therapy referral partner for children?

catchers.hypo: I run a community space, library or bookshop and want a calm music event for families with sensory needs.
catchers.can: I can plan and lead a sensory-friendly music session or info talk.
catchers.confirm: Is this a free or low-cost family event for a group of children and parents, with a quiet, safe setting?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired nurse or health worker who knows families of newly diagnosed kids and would like to help point them somewhere good.
catchers.can: Through my mum, a retired nurse who is supportive of the practice, I can reach health-care networks and pass on the parent group or practice information.
catchers.confirm: Do you have contact with families of newly diagnosed children in or near Toronto and want to share information about a local program?

catchers.hypo: I'm a school teacher with students who respond to music, and I'd like to learn some simple tools for the classroom.
catchers.can: I can offer simple music-based techniques, or point teachers to a workshop I could run.
catchers.confirm: Are you a teacher who wants practical music-based strategies for students with autism, not a full therapy program?

catchers.hypo: I make or sell small furniture and rugs, and I could give a new small practice a good deal.
catchers.can: I can use a rug, curtains or a small cabinet, with no nails in the walls.
catchers.confirm: Can the items be secondhand or inexpensive and delivered to a second-floor room in Leslieville?

forbids.text: I don't take clients without a clear safety plan.
I can't do Thursday evening sessions.
I won't share any client identities or details.
I won't share details about referrals from my hospital work.
I can't take on commitments that push my rent above $1,200 a month or my setup budget past its limit.

projects.name: Parent group pilot
projects.text: A monthly Saturday-morning singing-and-talking group for parents of newly diagnosed children, free for the first three sessions.

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share my equipment needs, budget limits and current client load.
policy.t2: Once the match is strong and I trust the other party, I'll share how I feel about money and my personal life.
policy.never: Client identities and details of hospital referrals.
